intro: A sector is the part of a circle between two radii, like a slice of pizza. A segment is the part between a chord and its arc. We find their areas and arc lengths as a fraction (θ/360°) of the whole circle.
keyPoints: Area of a circle = πr², circumference = 2πr.
A sector of angle θ is θ/360 of the whole circle.
Area of segment = area of sector − area of the triangle formed by the two radii and the chord.
Use π = 22/7 when the radius is a multiple of 7, otherwise 3.14 unless told.

examples.title: Area of a sector
examples.problem: Find the area of a sector of a circle of radius 7 cm with angle 90°. (π = 22/7)

examples.title: Length of an arc
examples.problem: Find the length of the arc of a circle of radius 21 cm that subtends 60° at the centre. (π = 22/7)

examples.title: Clock problem
examples.problem: The minute hand of a clock is 14 cm long. Find the area swept by it in 5 minutes. (π = 22/7)
steps: In 60 minutes it turns 360°, so in 5 minutes it turns 30°.
